title: Soča Valley & Goriška Brda Gravel Week

bestPeriod.avoid: November-March, Kolovrat ridge roads ice or snow-block and most Kobarid guesthouses close

accommodation.note: Kobarid guesthouses €70, €110 pppn; Brda wine estates €110, €145

food.note: Gostilna mains €12, €18; one Hiša Franko blowout adds €150, €300

transport.note: Airport transfer, Bohinj railway leg, luggage shuttle Kobarid→Brda

activities.note: Gravel hire €210, €260/week, Kobarid Museum €8, two winery tastings €40

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5, six riding days of 900-1,800 m ascent with sustained 9-12% gravel ramps on the Kolovrat side roads

gatewayAirport: TRS Trieste-Ronchi dei Legionari, 75 min drive to Kobarid; LJU Ljubljana 1 h 50 min; VCE Venice 2 h 15 min
summary: Two textures in one week. The first half climbs repeatedly out of Kobarid onto the Kolovrat ridge, a militarised limestone spine where Isonzo Front trenches still cut the grass and tarmac gives way to white dolomite without warning. The second half drops 900 m into Goriška Brda, where gradients shorten but never stop, hills are terraced in ribolla gialla, and the Italian border is a line you cross four times a day. It suits riders who like climbing in 6-14 km doses on 40-45 mm tyres. Distances stay at 55-80 km because the ascent-per-kilometre ratio is punishing.

itinerary.title: Landing in Kobarid, legs open on the Napoleon bridge loop
itinerary.morning: Transfer from Trieste to Kobarid and collect the gravel bike from Positive Sport on Mučeniška ulica, insisting on a 40 mm minimum tyre. Walk ten minutes to the Kobarid Museum for the Isonzo Front context that makes every ridge this week legible.
itinerary.afternoon: Shakedown loop: Kobarid, the Napoleon bridge, the Drežnica turn, Trnovo ob Soči and back on the right bank, dipping to the Great Soča Gorge.
itinerary.evening: Hiša Polonka on Gregorčičeva, Ana Roš's casual room. Order the frika with Tolminc cheese and a glass of Movia.
itinerary.dayStats: 34 km / 480 m ascent / 90% paved, 10% gravel access track / max gradient 9%

itinerary.title: Kolovrat ridge, the week's hardest hour
itinerary.morning: Roll south to Volarje and start the Kolovrat ascent via Selišče. The first 5 km are steepest; settle into a gear you can hold for 75 minutes. Tarmac ends above Ježa.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the crest gravel west to the Kolovrat Outdoor Museum at 1,114 m, restored Italian third-line trenches, tunnels and observation posts, Julian Alps one side, Friulian plain the other. Continue to the Solarji saddle, then descend the paved Livek road to Kobarid.
itinerary.evening: Topli Val at Hotel Hvala for Soča trout and the Brda white list.
itinerary.dayStats: 61 km / 1,780 m ascent / 65% paved, 35% dolomite gravel / summit 1,114 m / 12.8 km at 7.9%

itinerary.title: Vršno hairpins and the Tolminka gorge
itinerary.morning: Warm up on the left-bank road to Kamno, then take the Vršno switchbacks, eleven turns, 340 m, the poet Simon Gregorčič's birthplace at the top. Descend the same way.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride to Tolmin and walk the Tolminska korita gorge circuit, roughly 90 minutes past the Devil's Bridge and the wedged Bear's Head boulder. Then a gravel loop up Zatolmin toward Čadrg.
itinerary.evening: Gostilna Zatolmin outside Tolmin for štruklji and grilled meat at half Kobarid prices.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km / 1,250 m ascent / 70% paved, 30% gravel / Vršno 3.9 km at 8.7%, max 14%

itinerary.title: Most na Soči, the Bača valley, transfer south to Brda
itinerary.morning: Take the quiet right-bank road via Idrsko and Kred to Most na Soči, where the dammed Soča turns mint green, then the Bača valley spur toward Grahovo.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the Kanalski Lom ridge to Dobrovo, or shorten it with one stop on the Bohinj railway. Cross into Brda by the Neblo road; the landscape becomes terraced vine inside a kilometre.
itinerary.evening: Klinec in Medana for macerated ribolla and slow-cooked lamb. Book three days ahead, one sitting only.
itinerary.dayStats: 72 km / 1,120 m ascent / 80% paved, 20% hardpack / bike-on-train €3, paid on board

itinerary.title: Brda hill circuit: Šmartno, Medana, Ceglo, Vipolže
itinerary.morning: The ridge road from Šmartno to the Gonjače lookout tower, then drop and climb repeatedly through Kozana, Medana and Plešivo. Nothing is long; everything is 8-12%.
itinerary.afternoon: Two tastings, no more, Marjan Simčič at Ceglo for the Opoka single-vineyard whites, then Ščurek at Plešivo for Stara Brajda and the sculpture park. Recover on the flat cypress avenue at Vipolže.
itinerary.evening: Gredič at Ceglo for the tasting menu, or the cheaper terrace at Hiša Marica.
itinerary.dayStats: 64 km / 1,340 m ascent / 75% paved, 25% vineyard hardpack / no climb over 3 km but 22 ramps above 8%

itinerary.title: Cross-border day: Collio, Cormòns and Nova Gorica
itinerary.morning: Drop west into Italian Collio via Vipolže, identical geology, different signage. Ride the Plessiva ridge above Cormòns, then the vine lanes through Ruttars and Lonzano.
itinerary.afternoon: Loop east to Nova Gorica and roll across Trg Evrope / Piazza Transalpina, the square split by the border where the twin cities ran their joint European Capital of Culture year in 2025.
itinerary.evening: Belica in Medana, a farm restaurant with a terrace over the vines; order the cherry dishes in late May and June.
itinerary.dayStats: 78 km / 1,180 m ascent / 88% paved, 12% gravel / two Schengen border crossings, no checks

itinerary.title: Sabotin, Solkan and out
itinerary.morning: Final climb: Sabotin from Solkan, 6.7 km at 7.2% to 609 m, a WWI battleground with summit tunnels and the best single view of the Soča leaving the mountains.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to Solkan for the stone arch railway bridge, at 85 m, the longest stone arch span ever built for a railway. Return the bike via the pre-arranged shuttle to Positive Sport.
itinerary.evening: Hiša Franko in Kobarid, which retained three Michelin stars in the 2026 guide. Book three to six months ahead.
itinerary.dayStats: 46 km / 780 m ascent / 95% paved / Sabotin 6.7 km at 7.2%, summit 609 m
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Hvala, Kobarid, or an airport hotel at Ronchi

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Hvala
accommodationStrategy.description: Combines a secure ground-floor bike room, breakfast from 07:00 for early Kolovrat starts, and Topli Val downstairs. Around €95, €130 double B&B, two minutes from Positive Sport for a mid-week mechanical.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hiša Marica
accommodationStrategy.description: Inside Šmartno's walled medieval core, so you ride out of a village gate straight into vineyards. The cellar locks around six bikes, there is an outdoor tap for washing, and the terrace kitchen saves you descending to Dobrovo after a hard day. Roughly €110, €145 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Nebesa Chalets
accommodationStrategy.description: The luxury option at 700 m directly above the Livek climb: your morning is an 8 km descent, your evening an 8 km penalty. Glass-fronted cabins, shared sauna, dinner included, roughly €280, €340 per cabin.

logistics.connectivity: 4G is solid on the valley floor and in Brda, patchy on the Kolovrat crest, absent in the Bača side valleys. EU roaming applies. Load offline tiles: the gravel forks at Solarji are badly signed.
logistics.emergency: 112 covers GRZS mountain rescue on Kolovrat. Slovenia honours EHIC/GHIC but recovery costs may not be, carry sports insurance naming off-road cycling. Nearest hospital: Šempeter pri Gorici, 45 min from Kobarid.
logistics.weather: One of Europe's wettest basins; storms build over the Krn massif from 14:00 in June and September. In autumn the burja accelerates through the Vipava and Brda gaps at 80-120 km/h and stops you dead on exposed ridges. Check meteo.si daily.
logistics.bookingWindows: Hiša Franko three to six months. Klinec and Belica three to five days. Positive Sport gravel bikes six weeks for June weekends. Hiša Marica two months for September.
logistics.money: Slovenia is in the eurozone. Cards work almost everywhere, but mountain gostilnas above Livek and the Kolovrat hut are cash-only. Tipping means rounding up, or 10% for a full meal.
logistics.transportRules: A Slovenian e-vinjeta (€16 weekly) is required if your car uses the A1/H4, buy online before crossing. Bikes on trains cost €3 per journey, no advance reservation. Cross-border rental into Italy is generally free; into Croatia it usually is not. Carry ID for Schengen crossings.
logistics.permits: Triglav National Park lies north of the route, so its rules do not bite, but the Kolovrat trenches are protected heritage: no metal detecting, no removing objects, and unexploded WWI ordnance still surfaces. Drones need Slovenian CAA registration and are banned over the Kobarid Museum and military cemeteries.
logistics.health: Tap water is drinkable throughout, fountains included. Ticks on Kolovrat grassland April-October are the real hazard: Slovenia has one of Europe's highest tick-borne encephalitis rates, so consider vaccination and check nightly. The Soča runs 8-12°C in August, cold shock, not depth, is the swimming risk.

proTips: Climb Kolovrat on a weekday before 08:00, the ridge gravel stays shaded until mid-morning and the motorcyclists who own the Livek-Solarji road do not appear before eleven.
The Solarji crossing drops you into Italy on an unsigned dirt road toward Clabuzzaro on far worse tarmac. Ride out and back on the Slovenian side unless you are on 45 mm+ tyres.
Tell Positive Sport your frame model when booking and ask them to fit a spare rear mech hanger. Nothing between Tolmin and Nova Gorica will stock one.
Brda tastings are farm visits, not tasting rooms. Phone or email a day ahead; arriving unannounced at Simčič or Ščurek on a Tuesday gets you a locked gate.
Buy the €3 bike ticket the second the conductor appears at Most na Soči, the Bohinj railway carriages cap bikes at a handful, first come first served.
The Brda cherry harvest peaks in the first fortnight of June with open-cellar weekends. Best riding of the year, and also when Šmartno beds vanish first.
Refill at the public fountain on Šmartno's square; the Brda ridge has almost no shade and 64 km there drinks like 100 km elsewhere.
Carry €40 cash for the Kolovrat and Livek huts. They serve outstanding jota and none of them takes cards.

raw.Signature climb, Kolovrat from Tolmin vi: 12.8 km, 1,010 m ascent, 7.9% average, 15% maximum on the Selišče hairpins, cresting at 1,114 m at the Kolovrat Outdoor Museum. Tarmac to Ježa, then 4 km of graded white gravel along the ridge.
raw.Livek pass from Kobarid: 8.4 km, 470 m, 5.6% average, summit 679 m, fully paved, the warm-up and the gateway to the Solarji border ridge at 1,000 m via 6 km of packed forest gravel.
raw.Vršno hairpins: 3.9 km, 340 m, 8.7% average with two 14% ramps out of Kamno; eleven switchbacks, all paved, dropping straight to the river.
raw.Week surface split: approximately 62% paved (narrow, chip-sealed, near-empty), 28% white dolomite and forest hardpack, 8% vineyard farm track, 2% short singletrack link at Most na Soči. A 40-45 mm gravel tyre is the correct tool; 32 mm road rubber costs you the two best days.
raw.Bike hire: Positive Sport, Mučeniška ulica 8B, Kobarid (+386 40 821 810) is the valley's main rental and workshop, gravel, MTB and e-MTB, roughly €35, €45/day gravel and €50, €60 e-bike, weekly €210, €260, free bike-box storage for hirers. Marko Munih's shop at Cankarjeva ulica 3, Tolmin (+386 5 3811 464) covers spares and wheel-truing; Outdoor Galaxy (Ledina 1, Bovec) and Soča Experience (Čezsoča 129) serve the upper valley. One-way drop-off in Brda is not standard, budget a €40, €60 recovery fee.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation: Hotel Hvala and Nebesa Chalets both give locked ground-floor bike storage; Hiša Marica in Šmartno stores bikes in the stone cellar with an outdoor tap for washing. No property here has a full workshop stand, carry a multitool and a spare mech hanger.
raw.Bike on public transport: Slovenske železnice charges €3 per bicycle per journey, paid to the conductor on board; no reservation is possible and space is genuinely limited, so avoid 06:00-08:00 and 14:00-16:00 weekday peaks. The Bohinj railway from Most na Soči is the useful line. Bikes are barred from ICS Pendolino services. Italian regional trains out of Gorizia charge €3.50 for a 24-hour bike ticket.
